newsitem.title: UK: Woman cleared of bombing Israel's London embassy.
newsitem.headline: Woman cleared of bombing Israel's London embassy.

text.p: A Palestinian woman accused of bombing Israel's London embassy walked free from court on Monday when a judge ruled there was not enough evidence against her.
BBC television news said Nadia Zekra, 49, would formally be cleared on Tuesday when the judge would instruct the jury to find her not guilty.

"Since the arrest I was always thinking that this has to come to an end because I'm innocent... I know nothing about what they were talking about," she told the BBC outside London's Central Criminal Court.
The prosecution had claimed that the London housewife drove the car carrying the bomb to the embassy in 1994.
The only evidence against her came from a guard outside the embassy, but the judge said his description of a fairly tall, stocky woman did not match Zekra's appearance.

The case against another woman and two men charged with conspiracy and possession of firearms and explosives allegedly connected with the embassy attack will continue on Tuesday. The three have denied the charges.
They are also accused of taking part in a second attack in which a bomb exploded outside a Jewish charitable organisation in north London.
No-one was injured in the attack on the Israeli embassy, but the building was badly damaged and windows were shattered in nearby houses.
The embassy bomb was set off after then Israeli prime minister Yitzhak Rabin and King Hussein of Jordan signed the Washington Declaration paving the way for peace between their countries.
